newsitem.title: USA: New allegations against Maine nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: New allegations against Maine nuclear plant.

text.p: Nuclear Regulatory Commission officials said Friday they were probing allegations that the Maine Yankee nuclear plant improperly altered the findings of a 1992 safety analysis.

The charges are contained in two-page letter with five volumes of supporting documents given to the Union of Concerned Scientists by an anonymous whistleblower. The group turned the information over to the NRC on Thursday.
"We will be in contact with the UCS to determine if there is more information they can provide to us, to help us, but we will be acting very promptly on this," said NRC spokeswoman Diane Screnci.

Maine Yankee spokeswoman Maureen Brown said officials at the Wiscasset, Maine, facility were unaware of the new allegations until contacted by the news media but said they would fully cooperate in any investigation.
It would be a violation of federal law to knowingly supply the NRC with misinformation about the plant's safety, Screnci said.

The Justice Department and the NRC are already probing a 1995 whistleblower's allegations that Maine Yankee engineers improperly manipulated testing on the emergency core cooling system (ECCS) in the late 1980s.

The new letter alleges engineers made other key operating systems appear safer than they actually were, and based some risk analysis on modifications to the 25-year-old facility that had not actually been implemented.

The new whistleblower said that if the allegation about the ECCS are also true, "then it is possible to conclude that Maine Yankee at full power is one of the more dangerous plants on the North American continent," according to a copy of the letter obtained by Reuters.

Maine Yankee has had been plagued by equipment problems and safety allegations for the past three years. Its latest outage began on Dec. 6 when officials discovered many key electrical cables had been misrouted.
The plant's owners have been discussing a purchase of the facility by Peco Energy Corp., and said it will likely be closed if a deal cannot be completed by early fall.
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co., 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities and 22 percent by other New England utilities.
